_note: Chapter quiz questions shown in the app. The right answers live only on the server (functions/learn.py); scripts/learn_test.py checks the two match.

opts: A loan you give to a bank
A small piece of a company
basics.why: A share is a small piece of a company. Own a share of Apple and you own a sliver of Apple.

basics.q: You buy 5 shares at $20. The price rises to $24. What is your profit?
basics.why: Each share went up $4, and you have 5 of them: 5 × $4 = $20.

basics.q: You want to buy only if the price drops to $45. Which order fits?
basics.why: A limit buy only fills at your price or lower.

basics.q: Your account is $10,000: $7,500 in stocks and $2,500 cash, no orders waiting. Your buying power is about…
basics.why: Buying power is the cash you can spend; the rest is already in stocks.

basics.q: A company beats its earnings estimate but the stock falls. The most likely reason?
basics.why: Prices reflect expectations. If people hoped for more, even a beat can disappoint.

risk.q: Before buying, a planned trade should have…
opts: An entry, a stop and a target
risk.why: Know where you get in, where you’re wrong and where you take profit before you buy.

risk.q: Entry $40, stop $38, target $46. The reward-to-risk is…
You’ll risk $200. Entry $50, stop $46. How many shares?
Bad news overnight and the stock opens far below your stop. Your stop…
opts: Sells at exactly your stop price
Sells at the next available price, which can be much lower
risk.why: Stops can’t jump gaps: they sell at the next price available.

risk.q: An account falls 50%. To get back to even it needs…
risk.why: From half back to whole is a 100% gain. Avoiding big losses matters most.

opts: The price closed higher than it opened
The price closed lower than it opened
charts.why: Red means the price ended that period lower than it started.

charts.q: You’re up $300 on a stock you still hold. That profit is…
charts.why: Until you sell, P&L is unrealized and moves with the price.

charts.q: A $100 stock falls 10% to $90, then rises 10%. Where does it end up?
charts.why: 10% of $90 is $9, so it ends at $99. A rise is worked out on the smaller price, so it doesn’t fully make up the fall.

charts.q: A stock is up 3% today. You bought at $80 and it’s now $70. Are you in profit on it?
opts: No, you’re still below your cost
charts.why: Profit is measured from your cost, not today’s move.

charts.q: Higher highs and higher lows on a chart describe…
charts.why: Rising highs and rising lows are the definition of an uptrend.

signals.why: Indicators summarise what already happened, so they lag.

signals.q: MACD crossing above its signal line is usually read as…
signals.why: It’s a bullish momentum sign, never a guarantee.

signals.q: A breakout on very low volume is…
opts: More likely to fail than one on heavy volume
signals.why: Heavy volume shows broad agreement; thin breakouts fail more often.

opts: One estimate of where it could go; it may not
signals.why: Targets are estimates, often wrong. Use them as context.

signals.q: Your price alert at $200 goes off. You now…
signals.why: An alert only tells you. An order is what actually buys or sells.

patterns.q: In a head and shoulders, the usual confirmation is…
patterns.why: The neckline break confirms it; before that it’s only possible.

patterns.q: A double bottom confirms when price…
opts: Rises above the high between the two lows
patterns.why: The break above the middle high is the confirmation.

patterns.q: Which triangle has a flat top and rising lows?
patterns.why: Flat ceiling, higher lows: ascending, often read as bullish.

opts: A pause after a sharp rise that often continues up
patterns.why: A short, orderly pause in a strong uptrend.

patterns.q: Price breaks above resistance, then quickly falls back below it. That is…
patterns.why: When a break snaps back, it’s a false breakout; a stop limits the cost.

options.why: One contract is 100 shares, so a $2 price costs $200.

options.q: You buy a call. You make money when the stock…
options.why: Calls gain when the stock rises, especially above the strike.

options.q: The stock is at $95. A $100 put is…
options.why: A put is in the money when the stock is below the strike.

options.q: With the stock unchanged for a week, an option usually…
options.why: Time value melts away each day.

options.q: An option that is out of the money at expiration is worth…
options.why: Out of the money at expiration means it expires worthless.

options-manage.q: You paid $2.00 and the option is now $3.00. You’re up…
Time decay hurts an option fastest…
opts: In the last days before expiration
options-manage.why: Decay speeds up sharply near expiration.

options-manage.q: After earnings, implied volatility drops. Option prices usually…
options-manage.why: Lower IV means cheaper options: the IV crush.

options-manage.q: You hold 5 contracts and sell 2. What happens?
options-manage.why: Selling some contracts closes only those.

options-manage.q: A call and a put of the same size on the same stock, when the stock rises…
opts: The call gains, the put loses

adv-stocks.q: Why buy a retest of a breakout level?
opts: A tighter, clearer stop just below the level
adv-stocks.why: It gives a logical, close stop. It can still fail.

adv-stocks.q: Five chip stocks in one account are risky because…
adv-stocks.why: Correlated positions act like one big bet.

adv-stocks.q: A safer way to add to a position is…
opts: Adding as it moves your way, raising the stop
adv-stocks.why: Add to strength and keep the total risk fixed.

adv-stocks.q: The usual trade-off of a hedge is…
opts: Less downside for some cost or less upside
adv-stocks.why: Protection costs money, upside, or both.

adv-stocks.q: A trading journal mainly helps you…
adv-stocks.why: Reviewing your reasons shows what to repeat and what to stop.

adv-options.q: A protective put on shares you own…
opts: Limits losses below the strike, for a cost
adv-options.why: It’s insurance: protection below the strike, paid with the premium.

adv-options.q: The main trade-off of a covered call is…
opts: Income now, but gains above the strike are capped
adv-options.why: You’re paid now but give up upside, and still own the downside.

adv-options.q: Selling a cash-secured put means you may have to…
opts: Buy the shares at the strike
adv-options.why: If the stock falls below the strike, you must buy at the strike.

adv-options.q: You sold 3 of 4 profitable contracts. The one left is…
opts: A runner that can still lose its value
adv-options.why: Banking profit on the others reduces the trade’s risk, but the runner can still go to zero.

adv-options.q: Why give a runner its own exit rule?
opts: So it doesn’t ride back to a loss
adv-options.why: Without a rule a runner can give back far more than planned.

mind.q: After a big loss yesterday, a healthy plan today is…
opts: Double your size to win it back
Trade your normal plan and size
mind.why: Chasing losses is revenge trading; normal size protects you.

mind.q: A stock is up 40% and you feel you must buy now. That’s…
opts: FOMO: slow down and check your plan

mind.q: You followed your plan and hit your stop. That trade was…
opts: Bad luck you must fix today
mind.why: A planned, small loss is part of trading.

mind.q: Why might a trader change chart colours?
opts: To make moves feel less alarming
mind.why: Calmer colours can make the same data easier to read calmly.

mind.q: Doing well with virtual money means…
opts: You’ll do the same with real money
Good habits, but real money feels harder; start small
mind.why: Practice builds habits; real money brings stronger emotions.
